subject: Trajectory calibration & QBR readout — scope resets and dependency asks
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Trajectory calibration & QBR readout — scope resets and dependency asks

Team —

Quick mid-quarter pulse before we finalize the QBR pack next week. I pulled together a short readout (attached) with where we sit against the leadership-level commitments. High-level: two initiatives are off-runway unless we secure a small set of infra and product dependencies this week.

Top asks (short):
- Infra: short-lived dedicated GPU for a 3-day stress validation of the new batching config (Platform Ops contact below). Needs approval by EOD Tue.
- Product: de-scope the lower-impact analytics widgets (OKR P2) from the external beta release so the customer-facing milestone stays intact. Need a final call from Karthik to confirm scope by Wed.
- CS / Customer: coordinate a one-hour sync with Finova to reset expectations if we change the beta ship date — Scott is available Thu morning.

What I need from each of you:
- Karthik: confirm the scope pivot and callout any downstream work your team will need (MBR, docs, migration notes).
- Naomi: give a 24-hour runbook for the proposed batching test and sign-off on which infra we can borrow.
- Markus: do you have bandwidth to lead the exec-facing slide for the QBR? I can draft, but prefer you to own the deck visuals.
- Monica: please draft a short customer message we can send to Finova if the ship date slips.

I highlighted timelines inside the attached trajectory-impact-matrix.xlsx. If we don't clear the infra ask by Wed EOD, I recommend we execute the scope pivot to preserve the external milestone.

Thanks —
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP, Product Strategy | Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- QBR_readout_notes_v1.pdf (summary of metrics and choices)
- trajectory-impact-matrix.xlsx (impact table + timeline)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trajectory calibration & QBR readout — scope resets and dependency asks

Lauren —

Thanks for the clear summary. I'm inclined to accept the scope pivot (drop the P2 analytics widgets from the external beta) to keep the customer milestone intact, assuming we do two things:

1) Publish a short migration note for customers explaining the phased feature rollout (Monica can draft).
2) Prioritize the deferred widgets on the next sprint so OSS/internal tooling isn't blocked.

Naomi — can you confirm the risk to our telemetry pipeline if we push the analytics work? If it's mostly dashboarding work, we can re-prioritize; if it touches core eventing, we need to flag it.

Markus — I'm OK if you own the QBR visuals; I'll provide the narrative bullets by Thu noon.

I'll mark the scope decision as "Accepted (pivot)" and update the tracking doc.

—Karthik
